key_insight: Input-state randomness can hide Trotter errors: the mean absolute observable-error bound for state 2-designs can be exponentially smaller in qubit count than the tight bound for state 1-designs.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for input-state statistics can sharpen quantum-simulation error estimates beyond worst-case bounds.
method: Compare observable-error bounds for state 1-designs and 2-designs.
Use excess frame potential to quantify second-moment deviations and identify sensitive accessible observables.
Extend the analysis to Hamiltonian trajectories with frame potential decaying as 1/T before saturation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical bounds, including a sufficient pth-order Trotter step count of O(T^(1+3/(4p))) under the stated trajectory behavior, rather than experimental benchmarks.
watch_item: The improved bounds depend on ensemble randomness and trajectory assumptions; they do not guarantee equally small errors for arbitrary inputs or observables.
paper_title: When Randomness Hides Quantum Simulation Errors
